title: Linux 7.3-rc2 Released Following Another Busy Week
summary: Linux 7.3-rc2 release candidate marks progress toward stable v7.3 kernel with active development cycle ongoing. For 5G RAN embedded developers, this release cycle introduces potential driver updates, networking stack improvements, and real-time performance enhancements critical for DU/CU workload optimization. Key focus: early testing of rc2 is essential to identify stability issues before production deployment in communication infrastructure.

title: Bootlin toolchains 2026.08 released
summary: Bootlin has released its 2026.08 version of free, pre-compiled cross-compilation toolchains. This update supports 43 CPU architectures, including various ARM, MIPS, and other embedded processor variants.

title: Three stable kernels for Monday
summary: Greg Kroah-Hartman released Linux kernel stable versions 7.2.4, 6.18.50, and 6.12.109 with critical fixes across the kernel tree. For embedded/5G firmware engineers, timely kernel updates are essential to patch security vulnerabilities and improve stability in RAN stack implementations. Immediate upgrade is recommended to maintain system integrity in production deployments.
raw_snippet:
Greg Kroah-Hartman has announced the release of the 7.2.4 , 6.18.50 ,
and 6.12.109 stable kernels. Each contains
important fixes throughout the tree. Users are advised to upgrade.

title: [$] Fixing the TCMalloc regression with RSEQ operations
summary: A kernel regression in version 6.19 broke TCMalloc allocator due to changes in restartable sequences (RSEQ), a lockless user-space synchronization mechanism that firmware code relies on for performance-critical sections. Embedded developers using memory allocators in high-frequency 5G signal processing pipelines must understand RSEQ behavior and validate allocator compatibility to prevent subtle race conditions and preemption-related failures.

if it is preempted over the course of an operation (and must, thus,

sequences broke the TCMalloc allocator ,

title: DirectX Support Promoted To Official Target Within LLVM
summary: The DirectX back-end within the LLVM compiler stack, backed by Microsoft, has been promoted to an officially supported target. This initiative enables compiling LLVM IR into DirectX Intermediate Language (DXIL) for Windows graphics drivers.
raw_snippet: Over the past four years there has been a lot of work on a DirectX back-end within the LLVM compiler stack. Microsoft has backed the initiative for being able to lower LLVM IR into the DirectX Intermediate Language (DXIL) for execution by Windows DirectX 12 graphics drivers. This back-end is now officially supported...

title: FEX 2609 Released With Speedier JIT Performance, JIT Disk Cache Option
summary: The FEX 2609 emulator has been released, introducing faster JIT performance and a disk cache option for running x86_64 binaries on ARM64 Linux systems. This release enhances compatibility and performance for applications on AArch64.
raw_snippet: FEX 2609 was released overnight as the newest monthly feature release for this open-source emulator that allows running Linux x86_64 binaries on AArch64, including the likes of Steam and Steam Play (Proton) for enabling Windows games to run rather well on ARM64 Linux systems...

title: LLVM Merges Support For AMD's RMPCHKD, RMPREAD & RMPOPT Instructions
summary: LLVM/Clang has added support for AMD's RMPCHKD, RMPREAD, and RMPOPT instructions for Zen 5 and newer processors. This prepares the compiler toolchain for incoming SEV-SNP virtualization optimizations in the Linux kernel.
raw_snippet: With the Linux kernel still working toward landing support for AMD's RMPOPT optimization for helping to reduce overhead on SEV-SNP enabled servers, the LLVM/Clang compiler has in turn prepped for the milestone by landing support for the RMPOPT, RMPREAD, and RMPCHKD instructions for Zen 5 and newer...

summary: Arm introduced the CSS for Mobile 2 platform, featuring C2-Ultra and C2-Pro CPUs with SME2 support alongside the Mali G2-Ultra NX GPU. This platform serves as an AI-native compute foundation utilizing the Armv9-A architecture.

title: YuzukiNeko – A Linux-capable Allwinner F101 RISC-V SBC with Raspberry Pi Pico form factor
summary: YuzukiNeko is an open-source RISC-V SBC using Allwinner F101 SoC with 1.008 GHz C907 core, minimal PSRAM, and compact Pico form-factor, supporting MIPI DSI/RGB/LVDS display interfaces. For embedded engineers, this represents an accessible RISC-V development platform for prototyping low-power 5G control/edge compute applications, though the single-core architecture and limited memory require careful firmware optimization for real-time constraints.
raw_snippet: YuzukiHD has made another open-source hardware Linux SBC. YuzukiNeko is a Raspberry Pi Pico-sized single board computer powered by a new Allwinner F101 RISC-V SoC. The Allwinner F101 processor features a single 1.008 GHz C907 RISC-V core, 8MB or 16 MB PSRAM, and support for various display interfaces such as MIPI DSI, 24-bit RGB, and LVDS.
